look_here_first: SIXWEEKS FESCUE — FIRST find a short-lived cool-season ANNUAL with shallow fibrous roots, threadlike rolled/folded blades about 0.5–1 mm wide, and a narrow usually contracted 1–20 cm panicle. Under a lens count 5–17 florets in one 4–10 mm spikelet, not spikelets in the panicle. Lower glume 1.7–4.5 mm/1 vein; upper glume 2.7–6.7 mm/3 veins; fertile lemma 2.7–6.5 mm/5 veins, ending in a real 0.3–6 mm awn. True ligule a very short 0.5–1 mm hairless-edged membrane. Compare the larger, persistent PERENNIAL Texas fescue with 2–4-flowered, awnless/mucronate spikelets; source photographs do not prove the hidden root or ligule.

best_field_traits: Native North American cool-season ANNUAL, often only ~8–40 cm tall and short-lived.
Very fine leaves commonly 1–2 mm wide, often folded or rolled.
Narrow erect panicle, often 3–16 cm long with short appressed branches.
Spikelets usually ~5–10 mm with several (5–13) small florets, each fertile lemma awned.
True ligule very short (~0.5 mm); mature awn/glume length variable across varieties and sources.
Synonym Vulpia octoflora (Walter) Rydb. in many references; no duplicate species admission.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Small entire annual tuft with rooted base and fine leaves
Spikelet floret count and mature awn lengths beside calibrated ruler
Pair of unequal glumes showing 1 vs 3 nerves
crew_field_check: Start from whole rooted plant to establish growth form.
Photograph flowering head and collar on same individual.
Use hand-lens/25x macro to measure floret structure when needed; photos without it support only provisional source determination.
Taxon synonym Vulpia octoflora is the same installed Festuca octoflora concept, not a new species admission. Texas fescue specific county occurrence not audited.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Festuca versuta (Texas fescue) is a perennial rather than a 6-weeks spring annual, with a more open branching flowering panicle in mature plants and a persistent base. The existing F. versuta image is loose seed/lemma material, so it does not prove panicle or perennial habit. For other Vulpia spp., dissect unequal glumes and measure lemma and awn instead of using dried color.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form: Cool-season annual, culms 10–60 cm; shallow fibrous-rooted; blades often inrolled, 0.5–1 mm wide.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.panicle: Contracted, often one-sided narrow panicle 1–20 cm (broad published range); branches generally appressed.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet: 4–10 mm, laterally compressed, usually 5–17 fertile florets with uppermost reduced; rachilla internodes may become visible at maturity.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.lower_glume: 1.7–4.5 mm, 1-veined, generally 60–70% length of upper glume.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.fertile_lemma: 2.7–6.5 mm, 5-veined, single terminal awn about 0.3–6 mm (Kew GrassBase); do not confuse awn with upper-glume tip.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.ligule_collar: True eciliate membranous ligule 0.5–1 mm; auricles not documented by existing image. Expose actual blade-sheath junction and measure.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.evidence_note: Published ranges vary across source treatments and individuals; neither photo independently proves every micromorphological feature.

crew_lookalike_key_20261023: Festuca versuta (Texas fescue): established PERENNIAL with 50–100 cm culms, open drooping 8–30 cm panicle, 2–4 florets per 6–9 mm spikelet and awnless or mucronate 5–7 mm lemmas. Require actual root/crown and mature spikelets.
Other Vulpia/Festuca annuals: a narrow awned panicle is not unique; measure both unequal glumes, 5-veined lemma, its awn, and floret number on the same mature spikelet.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SPLIT THE FESCUES
field_id_short_tiles.details: Festuca versuta has a persistent perennial crown, open drooping 8–30 cm panicle, 2–4 florets per 6–9 mm spikelet and awnless/minutely pointed lemmas. Sixweeks has a crowded narrow head, many more florets and actual lemma awns. Require attached rooted base and mature dissected spikelet before a difficult ID; preserve Vulpia octoflora as a synonym, not another installed species.
